lines.text: Why does a mill pay ₹8 more a kilo for some iron?
lines.tts: Why does a mill pay eight rupees more a kilo for some iron?
lines.phonemes: wˌaɪ dˈʌz ɐ mˈɪl pˈeɪ ˈeɪt ɹˈuːpiːz mˈɔːɹ ɐ kˈiːloʊ fɔːɹ sˌʌm ˈaɪɚn?

lines.text: The answer is inside the furnace.
lines.phonemes: ðɪ ˈænsɚɹ ɪz ɪnsˈaɪd ðə fˈɜːnɪs.

lines.text: Thin, rusty sheet oxidises away; thick, clean pieces return more steel.
lines.tts: Thin, rusty sheet oxidizes away; thick, clean pieces return more steel.
lines.phonemes: θˈɪn, ɹˈʌsti ʃˈiːt ˈɑːksɪdˌaɪzᵻz ɐwˈeɪ; θˈɪk, klˈiːn pˈiːsᵻz ɹᵻtˈɜːn mˈɔːɹ stˈiːl.

lines.text: So mills pay by grade: punchings top, light scrap last.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ mˈɪlz pˈeɪ baɪ ɡɹˈeɪd: pˈʌntʃɪŋz tˈɑːp, lˈaɪt skɹˈæp lˈæst.

lines.text: Keep heavy pieces apart, dry and free of dirt.
lines.phonemes: kˈiːp hˈɛvi pˈiːsᵻz ɐpˈɑːɹt, dɹˈaɪ ænd fɹˈiː ʌv dˈɜːt.

lines.text: Same truck, same trip cost, but a tonne of punchings brings ₹8,000 more.
lines.tts: Same truck, same trip cost, but a ton of punchings brings eight thousand rupees more.
lines.phonemes: sˈeɪm tɹˈʌk, sˈeɪm tɹˈɪp kˈɔst, bˌʌt ɐ tˈʌn ʌv pˈʌntʃɪŋz bɹˈɪŋz ˈeɪt θˈaʊzənd ɹˈuːpiːz mˈɔːɹ.

lines.text: Mills pay for the steel they get back.
lines.phonemes: mˈɪlz pˈeɪ fɚðə stˈiːl ðeɪ ɡɛt bˈæk.

lines.text: Join WastePaisa and put your scrap to use.
lines.phonemes: dʒˈɔɪn wˈeɪst pˈaɪsɑː ænd pˌʊt jʊɹ skɹˈæp tə jˈuːz.
